solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pass on perhaps in Hebridean location

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written
say means for example, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone is told to forward something, maybe while staying at a spot in the Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' looks like one verb meaning forward, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, so a fair place name for this.

clue.text: Cameron, Andrew and Thomas Stearns initiators here?

definitions.text: Cameron, Andrew and Thomas Stearns initiators here?

indicators.note: initiators are the starting letters, so the first letter of each of the four names is taken

explanation.surface: Asks where Cameron Mackintosh, Andrew Lloyd Webber and T S Eliot all began something together.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical was produced by Cameron Mackintosh, composed by Andrew Lloyd Webber and based on poems by Thomas Stearns Eliot: the three men really were its initiators.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage musical created by those three collaborators is the show these initials spell out.

clue.text: Hear Liberal is on the square

parts.note: taken as written
a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, so square gives T

explanation.surface: A politician of the Liberal party is said to be honest and above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the square' looks like the idiom for honest; here 'on' only joins and 'square' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for listen or pay attention, as in 'list, list, O list' from Hamlet.

clue.text: As Henry's Chancellor after refusal?

indicators.note: after puts the chancellor's name behind the refusal

parts.note: no is a refusal
Sir Thomas More was Lord Chancellor to Henry VIII

explanation.surface: Asks what became of Henry VIII's Chancellor once he had refused the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas More refused to accept Henry VIII's break with Rome and was executed, so after his refusal he was no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means no longer existing, which is exactly More's fate after he defied the king.

clue.text: Ramshackle castle in Wick's old resident going back in time?

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the town of Wick in Caithness, with the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A tumbledown castle in Wick has an elderly resident who seems to be living in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resident' only links the surface to the definition. Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock hands moving the wrong way would figuratively turn the hours backwards, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Call over Conservative historian and poet

parts.note: to bell is to call or cry out, and a bell is a call to attention
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to summon a Tory writer of history and verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc wrote both histories and comic verse such as the Cautionary Tales.

clue.text: Devonian river and dock for missing female appointee

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon to Exeter
to dock is to cut short

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for female is dropped from the word for

explanation.surface: A Devon river and a dock are listed in place of an absent woman given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing female' removes F from 'for', leaving OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person appointed in a will to carry out its terms.

clue.text: State capital no great shakes

definitions.meaning: read literally, a small shaking or rocking motion rather than a big one

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a state capital as nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no great shakes' is the idiom for unremarkable, but here it means only a slight rocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Rock is the capital of Arkansas; a little rock is also a gentle sway, not a great shake.

clue.text: Monastery sheet needs handling again

parts.note: a chart is a sheet such as a map or diagram
to reuse something is to use or handle it again

explanation.surface: A monastery's paperwork has to be processed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: La Grande Chartreuse is the mother house of the Carthusian order of monks near Grenoble.

clue.text: Pair perhaps unwelcome in this trial marriage

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A couple might not be welcome in a trial marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a pair is a score of nought in both innings, which no batsman wants in an international fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair (two ducks) is an unwelcome cricket score in this kind of international fixture.

clue.text: Location to West send herd or heifers mad

indicators.note: send ... mad frames the fodder: to send something mad is to make it wild
mad completes the instruction that the herd and heifers be scrambled

explanation.surface: A farm out west is told to drive its cattle crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is split: 'send' before the fodder and 'mad' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county lies on the Welsh border in the west of England, a place famous for its cattle.

clue.text: Erstwhile partner works in return for bonus

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in return means the word for works is turned back to front

parts.note: works of art, so art

explanation.surface: A former partner's labour is repaid with a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added on top, much like a bonus payment.

clue.text: One lighting fire butler put out with claret

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butler lighting the fire is upset alongside the claret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighting fire' sounds domestic, but the fire is gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a round glows in flight, showing the gunner the path of the shots being fired.

clue.text: Weep about girl having argument in Steinbeck story

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for weep goes round the girl

parts.note: to cry is to weep
Anne is a girl's name
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A girl in a quarrel is wept over in a Steinbeck tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannery Row is John Steinbeck's 1945 novel set on Monterey's waterfront.

clue.text: Make perfect date for legal situation

parts.note: to crown something is to complete or perfect it
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Arranging the perfect date is presented as a legal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crown Court hears serious criminal cases in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal venue where criminal trials sit, so a place or situation of law.

clue.text: Girl denied introduction creates atmosphere

indicators.note: denied introduction means the opening letter of the name is taken away

parts.note: Laura is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl left out of the introductions changes the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or feeling surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Tees here required leave for clues to be rewritten

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of for clues are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: The setter Tees has to go away so the clues can be redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees' looks like the setter's name, but it is the plural of tee, the pegs from which golf balls are struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tees are found on the links, where each hole begins from a tee.

clue.text: One trained takes minute replacing power in electronic device

indicators.note: replacing means the minute letter goes in where the power letter was

parts.note: a computer is an electronic device
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A trained engineer installs a tiny part in place of the power unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes minute replacing power' swaps P for M; 'minute' looks like tiny but is the time unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter is a person who travels to work by train, so one trained there daily.

clue.text: City folk demanding fresh deliveries

parts.note: new means fresh
a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: Urban residents insist on fresh produce brought to their door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests shopping, but it is bowled balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the American metropolis are city dwellers of one particular city.

clue.text: Does spiritual work

definitions.meaning: the New Testament book recording the deeds of the Apostles

explanation.surface: Someone performs religious labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means performs; the book of the Bible is a sacred text recounting the Apostles.

clue.text: Dad, look at cartoon hero!

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A child urges their father to watch a cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating sailor is a classic animated star of comic strips and films.

clue.text: Put back into service on assignment to keep constant order

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the first pair holds the second

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a mission is an assignment
C is the constant for the speed of light
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone on a job must maintain consistent orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals a container. C as the speed-of-light constant and the Order of Merit are crossword conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommission a ship or building is to restore it to active use.

clue.text: Destructive god reportedly restrained

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for restrained is heard rather than read

parts.note: low-key means restrained or understated

explanation.surface: A god of destruction is said to be held back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse trickster deity brings about the death of Baldr and the chaos of Ragnarok.

clue.text: Script from ethnic Chinese daughter

parts.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: A manuscript comes from a Chinese man's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a person's handwriting, a style of script.

clue.text: Nonsense about Indy causes stir

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for nonsense goes round the paper

parts.note: rot is nonsense
the Indy is The Independent, the paper running the puzzle, so the setter's word for it is us

explanation.surface: Nonsense printed about this newspaper sparks a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indy' is The Independent's nickname; from inside the paper it calls itself US.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse someone or stir them into action.

clue.text: Drink to consume Australian Third Man retired as writer

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or going back, so the whole string is read backwards
to consume means to take inside, so the drink holds the Australian

parts.note: ale is a drink
Oz is slang for Australia
Harry Lime is the villain of the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: A drink is downed by an Australian cricketer who has stopped playing at number three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third Man' looks like a fielding position but is the Orson Welles film. 'retired' turns ALOZELIME round.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote the Rougon-Macquart cycle and 'J'accuse'.

clue.text: Weak goddess twisted round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for twisted goes about the goddess

parts.note: wry means twisted or distorted
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A feeble goddess is spun about.
explanation.definitionFit: Diluted drinks or feeble efforts are thin and watery, lacking strength.

clue.text: Playwright to marry sweetheart and breed

parts.note: to wed is to marry
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E
a kind is a breed or type

explanation.surface: A dramatist plans to wed their beloved and raise a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Wedekind was the German dramatist of Spring Awakening and the Lulu plays.
